subject: [SummitHealth] streaming chat tail latency + error spike during peak (p95/p99 surge)
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@summithealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: support@summithealth.com
Date: 2028-03-24T19:02:00-07:00
Subject: Production: streaming chat p99 spikes during peak window

Hi Jonas / Lauren,

Quick heads up — during our 18:30–19:00 PT peak this evening we saw a sharp rise in tail latency for the live chat feature backed by Redwood's hosted streaming endpoint. p95 climbed from ~220ms to 1.1s and p99 hit ~3.9s for ~17 minutes. We also observed a ~7% increase in 5xx errors and intermittent client disconnects (SSE). I attached the ingestion and connection logs — you can see time-aligned spikes.

This impacted a subset of high-concurrency sessions for our weekend clinic routing. Our team briefly switched traffic to a degraded polling fallback which restored nominal behavior. We need an urgent RCA and mitigation timeline — this is affecting on-call coverage and escalations from operations.

Can you confirm next steps and whether there's an immediate mitigation we can apply from the Redwood side?

Thanks,
Olivia Park
Head of Platform Ops
SummitHealth

Attachments: ingestion-stats-peak-20280324.csv, sse-connection-logs-03-24.txt

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@summithealth.com>, Mike Turner <mike.turner@summithealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-24T19:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: streaming chat p99 spikes during peak window

Olivia — thanks for the report and the attachments. We've ingested the logs and started a quick triage. Initial signals show sustained connection churn and a small spike in inflight request queue length on the hosted streaming fleet for your region.

Immediate steps we've pushed:
- Enabled a temporary rate-smoothing policy on your account to cap short-term burst concurrency.
- Increased autoscale aggressiveness for the streaming pool serving your tenant for 30 minutes.
- Flipped a routing rule to prefer a lower-latency AZ for new connections.

Those actions should reduce tail events while we investigate root cause. Can you confirm whether polling fallback is still enabled on your side (that will help us compare client vs server-side reconnects)?

I'll loop in Product and Runtime to run deeper checks on batching parameters, queue backpressure, and kernel saturation.

— Jonas Weber
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-24T19:33:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production: streaming chat p99 spikes during peak window

Team — quick escalation. SummitHealth saw a p99 tail jump and ~7% 5xx increase during their peak. They temporarily degraded to polling which reduced impact. We applied temporary smoothing and an AZ-pref rule, but we need a short RCA and a durable mitigation.

Ask: can Runtime (Aditya) check for kernel-level stalls, KV cache thrash, or a sudden change in average sequence length distribution that could have forced inefficient kernel paths? Hannah, can you surface related metrics (batch sizes, per-server queue depth, CPU/GPU tail utilization) and prepare a short exec-ready summary. Evelyn — this may need an SLA exception note for the account if the root cause is capacity-related.

Let's aim for an update to SummitHealth in 90 minutes.

- Lauren
Director, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-24T20:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: streaming chat p99 spikes during peak window — initial findings

Short findings from runtime triage (10:00–10:40 UTC):
- Kernel selection: a small subset (~3% of shards) started using a non-quantized kernel path due to a recently-introduced model variant promotion; that caused per-token compute to increase ~2.6x for long sequences (>1024 tokens).
- Batching: bursty connection spikes increased effective batch jitter; some servers saw a short-lived batch head-of-line delay where longer sequences blocked small-message flows.
- KV cache churn: SummitHealth's sessions had an uptick in session length and token reuse patterns changed (higher context window per conversation), causing cache eviction oscillation on a few hosts.

Mitigation applied:
1) Forced the affected shards back to the quantized kernel path (rollback of the variant promotion) — should reduce compute per token for long sessions.
2) Lowered max batch accumulation window for the streaming pool to reduce head-of-line blocking.
3) Enabled adaptive KV retention to reduce eviction thrash for active sessions.

We'll continue monitoring; initial telemetry shows p95 dropping back under 300ms within ~6 minutes after changes and p99 trending down. Preparing a short write-up for SummitHealth.

— Aditya Rao
Senior Runtime Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: heap-snapshot-20280324.json

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@summithealth.com>, Mike Turner <mike.turner@summithealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-25T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Production: streaming chat p99 spikes during peak window — short RCA and next steps

Hi Olivia / Mike — quick update and apology for the disruption. Summary: during your peak window we observed a confluence of factors that elevated compute and queuing on a small subset of streaming hosts which produced the p95/p99 regressions you saw. Root causes: a recent model-variant promotion that selected a heavier kernel for long-sequence traffic, bursty connection patterns that increased batch jitter, and KV-cache eviction oscillation due to longer session contexts.

What we did tonight (timeline):
- 19:20 PT: applied short-term smoothing and AZ-pref routing to reduce new connection pressure.
- 19:25 PT: runtime rollback of variant promotion for affected shards (forced quantized kernel).
- 19:28 PT: lowered batch accumulation window and enabled adaptive KV retention.

Impact: within ~6 minutes of the rollback and batching change, p95 returned to <300ms and p99 declined back toward baseline in monitored traffic. We will continue 72-hour elevated monitoring for this account and provide a post-mortem with action items.

Near-term action items we will deliver by EOD:
- Post-mortem doc with timeline and telemetry snapshots (link to JIRA RW-4883).
- A permanent safety rule to prevent non-quantized kernel promotion into streaming pools without canary traffic.
- Recommended client-side best practice: enable polling fallback for bursty clinic windows until the safety rule is in place.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute call to walk through the post-mortem and map mitigations to your runbook. Again, apologies for the incident — we take these regressions seriously.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference
